svg.title: Engine memory, cores and the copy ledger — 2026-09-19
svg.desc: An audit sheet: every thread and the core it claims, every copy the bytes of one tick undergo from NIC to strategy callback, the resident memory map, the cache-line layout of the POD types, and the build profile. It contradicts the one-copy-per-event doctrine printed on the older architecture sheet: counting every full-record memcpy, a tick costs three and a depth snapshot four. The E7 addendum at the foot carries the exec lane's own TX/RX ledger after the 2026-09-19 zero-copy pass.
svg.text: Memory, cores and the copy ledger

text.tspan: what the engine actually does with RAM and CPU
· read from crates/ at HEAD 1225651, 2026-09-19; the exec-lane addendum at the foot re-read at the E7 review · companion to
This sheet contradicts the doctrine line on the 2026-08-29 architecture sheet.
“one unavoidable copy per event” is not what the code does — counting every full-record memcpy, a tick costs three and a depth snapshot four.

svg.text: THE PATH OF ONE TICK — every hop the bytes take, and what happens to them there
Nine hops from the wire to a strategy callback. Four of them move no bytes at all. One is inside rustls and cannot be checked from here. The rest copy — and every one of those is unconditional.

text.tspan: the depth detour — a DepthTopK costs FOUR full-record copies, not one.
The L2 ladder is mutated in place from the wire delta (zero-copy), but

svg.text: the 192-byte snapshot out of those arrays (book-builder/src/ladder.rs:166-221) — copy #1 — before capture stages it (#2), the ring push takes it (#3) and the pop moves it again (#4). The older sheet's phrase “depth snapshots 192 B” reads as one copy of 192 bytes.
AND ON THE WAY OUT — the doctrine line never mentioned this path at all
PM live path only — the HL arm runs in on_idle
… and back out of the ring
handwritten cursor, no serde, no format!
PM signer; the HL Agent signature is 0 B/op (gate 54)
THE COPY LEDGER — every copy of the payload bytes, counted
no — io::Read is the only API
the one copy our code controls in hops 1–2
only when the tail pins full with dead head bytes
XOR in place over the same bytes
borrowed slice · no reassembly buffer exists
no serde_json, no String, no Vec anywhere
boot-built table · the lookup is alloc-free
depth only · NOT in the doctrine sentence
ALWAYS ON · runs BEFORE the ring push
this is the ONLY copy the doctrine names
outbound path, unaddressed by the doctrine
the Polymarket path only — the HL arm never crosses it
one pass, no heap, no format!
a budget test, not a 0 B/op assertion
documented in the source, and correct
documented in the source, and correct
Nothing on the ingest path touches the heap after boot — every copy above lands in storage that was allocated once, at startup, and is reused forever. That is the claim the code actually supports.

One copy = one full-record memcpy the process performs. A ring transfer is therefore TWO — the producer's ptr::write and the consumer's ptr::read — because the slot is reused on wraparound and cannot be handed out by reference.
capture stage → ring push → ring pop
ladder snapshot → capture stage → ring push → ring pop
capture + RecentRing; the HL arm renders from &Order in place on the engine thread — no hop-ring (see the foot)
file read → validator scratch → ring → VM ping-pong slot
The TLS plaintext copy sits underneath all of these: it is per-read, not per-record, and it is the only one our code could not remove even in principle.
THE VERDICT ON THE DOCTRINE LINE
“one unavoidable copy per event — the slot into the ring
(64 B; depth snapshots 192 B; RuleTable ferries by value…)”
A tick makes THREE full-record copies, not one
— the capture staging buffer, the ring push, and the ring pop.
Capture and the ring are independent destinations and capture
is unconditional. A depth snapshot costs four.
The RuleTable clause is the honest part
— two copies, at operator cadence, and the source says so
itself in the same words. Everything inbound is understated
by 3–4×; the outbound path is not described at all.
WHAT THE 0 B/op GATES ACTUALLY PROVE
alloc / dealloc calls and bytes. AllocGuard asserts the delta is zero
around a region. 62 such tests run under --test-threads=1.
they measure HEAP ALLOCATION, not memcpy volume.
A function that performs five copy_from_slice calls into
boot-allocated buffers reports 0 B/op, correctly. The suite
cannot be cited for or against “one copy per event” — it
six per-venue run-loop steady-state tests drive the real Driver
over scripted wire bytes — parse, capture and ring push are all
exercised for zero heap alloc, including OKX's DepthTopK path.
ruleset_table_handoff drives both RuleTable copies end to end.
gap: Bybit has no alloc-gate coverage at all.
bench/Cargo.toml lists 7 ingress crates and omits ingress-bybit.
No clippy lint enforces any of this — clippy.toml has no disallowed-methods list. The discipline is a runtime test, not a static gate.
THREADS AND CORES — what the process actually schedules
Engine::tick(256) · all 7 strategy slots evaluate in-line here
ONE THREAD AND ONE SOCKET PER SYMBOL — 254 at the 09-12 mark
OKX v5 public WSS + L2 book walk
Deribit JSON-RPC WSS + L2 book walk
HL public WSS — market data; the userFills socket lives on the ENGINE thread
the AI command plane — UDS listener, HMAC, seq, ruleset validator
pops the Order ring, calls the real dispatcher
ratatui dashboard, reads the same snapshot cell
the core map above describes intent; on the M4 deployment none of it binds

pin_current_thread_to_core() calls sched_setaffinity(2) on Linux and is kernel-enforced. On macOS pin_impl() is #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))] and returns Err(Unsupported) — one warning is logged and the thread floats (cli/src/pinning.rs:92-99).

No thread anywhere sets .stack_size(), so every one takes Rust's 2 MiB default. At the 254-socket mark that is ~265 threads reserving ~530 MiB of VIRTUAL address space; resident stack pages will be far smaller, and I could not measure them from source — that needs vmmap on the live process.
RESIDENT MEMORY — where the bytes live, allocated once at boot and never resized
≈ 53.6 MiB of clearly attributable heap at the 254-Binance-socket mark
network buffers are the volatile half: with a majors-only universe the total falls to ≈ 36 MiB
9.07 MiB total. Ring<T,N> head and tail each own a full
64 B cache line, so the producer and the consumer never
capture staging is the one ESTIMATED figure on this bar — roughly 20 PmlrCapture
instances × a 64 KiB buffer each; the exact instance count was not enumerated.
what is NOT in that 53.6 MiB
thread stacks — ~265 threads × 2 MiB default reservation ≈ 530 MiB of
VIRTUAL address space. Resident pages are lazily committed and almost
certainly far smaller, but nothing in the source can tell you how much.
the binary — 5.22 MiB on disk, stripped of debuginfo.
rustls internals — a 16 KiB received-plaintext cap per connection that
this codebase never sets itself; its ciphertext buffering is session-managed
and not a fixed allocation. The §5.4 backpressure incident lives here.
production runs the platform default allocator — no jemalloc, no mimalloc,
and CountingAllocator is installed in the bench test binary ONLY.
CACHE-LINE LAYOUT — every hot type is #[repr(C, align(64))] and size-asserted at compile time
RuleTableV2 = 256 rows × 128 B + one metadata line = 32 832 B · 513 cache lines. Deliberately NOT AsBytes: it is built in memory by the validator and never parsed from wire bytes.
padding that exists to stop false sharing, not to round a number:
core_ring::Padded — head and tail each get their own 64 B line (core-ring/src/lib.rs:66-77)
engine_snapshot::SnapshotCell — the seq counter sits on its own line ahead of the payload, so a polling reader never false-shares with the writer (cell.rs:32-39)
core_metrics::Counter — every metric counter is align(64), used pervasively across the engine_* families

SnapshotCell is a single-writer seqlock rather than a Mutex for a specific reason: Darwin's pthread mutex lazily heap-allocates pthread_mutex_t on first lock, which broke the zero-alloc gate on macOS.
repr(align(64)) appears in 34 files across the workspace — the convention is repo-wide, not per-crate.
clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW) — chosen so NTP slew cannot move it.
Read once per parsed inbound frame to stamp ts_ns, not once per loop pass.
LatencyTracker<24> ×3 — 1 536 log-linear buckets each, one atomic fetch_add
per record, percentile by cumulative scan. Lock-free and allocation-free.
The whole crate is one scalar byte_sum() plus two tests, and nothing
outside the crate references it. No AVX2 or NEON kernel exists; the
target-cpu flags below let LLVM auto-vectorise, and that is all.
no prefetch instructions exist anywhere in the tree.
Branchless patterns that do exist: TopOfBook::apply's gap count, head & (N-1)
in place of head % N, and symbol_bucket_mix's XOR fold. get_unchecked in the
ring's push and pop removes the bounds checks on the hot path.

text.tspan: The engine's real claim is not zero copies — it is
zero heap allocation after boot, and a bounded, counted number of copies into storage that was sized once
. That claim survives the audit intact.

svg.text: What does not survive is the arithmetic: capture and the ring are two independent, unconditional destinations; the ring transfer is itself two moves; and a depth snapshot is materialised out of the ladder before any of that happens. The honest sentence, for whoever writes the next doctrine line:

“Counting every full-record memcpy: a tick costs three — the PMLR capture stage, the ring push and the ring pop — with capture and the ring being independent, unconditional destinations. A depth event costs four, an order two

on either path (the HL arm signs and sends from the engine thread, with no hop-ring), and a RuleTable three at operator cadence. All of them land in boot-preallocated fixed-capacity storage; nothing on the ingest path touches the heap after startup. The Polymarket signer is the one exception, at ~208 B per signature — budgeted, not eliminated; the Hyperliquid Agent signature is 0 B/op.”

Every verdict above was established by reading the code, not the comments. Three stale comments were found and are worth fixing at the source: engine/src/lib.rs:64 says “five rings = 5 MiB” when NUM_TICK_LANES is 6 seventeen lines below; engine/src/lib.rs:690 calls the RuleTable slot “16 KiB” when it is 32 832 B; and cli/src/paper.rs:27 says cores 0..=7 are pinned when Bybit takes core 8.
E7 ADDENDUM — THE EXEC LANE'S OWN COPY LEDGER (read after the 2026-09-19 review + zero-copy pass)

The live arm (exec-hyperliquid) is driven from OrderDispatch::on_idle on the engine thread — not through the QueuedDispatcher hop-ring, which is the Polymarket path. The rule it was audited against: everything that can be zero-copy is; every remaining copy carries a // COPY: line; make copy-audit ratchets the exec lane + core-net against a 33-entry pre-E1 baseline.
TX — one live order · copies of the action / body bytes: 2 (TLS + kernel), the house target, plus the serialiser's one tolerated write
the serialiser's own write into the FINAL action buffer — keccak'd in place, never staged again
IN PLACE behind the head; the old envelope() copied the whole action JSON out of a scratch buffer per order — gone
action absorbed part by part; only the 8 B nonce + vault + expiry tail is built on the stack
typehash and keccak(source) cached; the 64 B r‖s secp256k1 hands back by value is the one copy (no serialise-into-slice API)
nonce + signature appended after the action; the body is complete in one buffer
two TLS segments (no body byte enters the header buffer); rustls plaintext → ciphertext, ciphertext → kernel — the two the doctrine allows
RX — one venue fill · copies: 3 (kernel + TLS + ring slot), the house target; the tail compaction is now a CURSOR
the same two boundary copies as every ingress socket; drained to WouldBlock (mio is edge-triggered)
a consumed frame ADVANCES rx_head — the first cut copy_within'd the unread tail after EVERY frame (O(k²) on a burst; the auditor caught it)
coin is a Span into rx, resolved by bytes against the roll-bound table — never a String, never parsed back into an asset id
the designed ring publish — the ONLY byte move the fill makes on its way to the engine loop
the pop and the capture stage, exactly as a tick; then &Fill by reference into the ledger and the strategy
only when the buffer is FULL with a partial frame behind consumed bytes (core_net::IoBuf's law); a fully drained buffer resets to 0 for free

Gates that pin this: bench gate 54 (encode + sign, 0 B/op), gate 58 (encode → envelope → scan), gate 60 (stage_modify + seal in the arm's own buffers), tests/hl_userws_loopback.rs (four scripted WS servers), make copy-audit (hits=33 baselined=33 new=0), and the zero-copy-auditor agent's own FAIL→fix on this sheet's rx cursor. Not on this sheet: strategy identities (never-in-git law).
